raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`Gemma4Router` folds `scale * root_size` into `norm.weight` on its first forward and sets `_scale_fused`, and nothing ever clears that flag. So after an online weight update (`update_weights_from_distributed`, `update_weights_from_tensor`, `update_weights_from_disk`) loads a new `scale`, the router keeps routing with the old one, with no error or warning.

We hit this while adding Gemma 4 to the SGLang weight sync in [Halo](https://github.com/whitecircle/halo), which carries a local patch for now. It's the same kind of bug as #35883 (GLM gate).

## Modifications

- `scale` gets its own weight loader that writes the parameter and refolds it into `norm.weight` in place, so CUDA graph replays see the new value too. Only clearing the flag wouldn't fix replays, because a replay doesn't run the `_scale_fused` check in `forward`.
- `fuse_scale` moves `scale` to the buffers' device first. With `--cpu-offload-gb`, `scale` is still on the CPU at load time while `root_size` is on the GPU.
- `forward` keeps its lazy fold for loads that skip `load_weights` (e.g. `--load-format dummy`).
- `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` and `gemma4_diffusion.py` load `scale` through the parameter's own loader, so they're fixed too.
- Not covered: `update_weights_from_tensor(load_format="direct")` skips parameter loaders, so the fold still goes stale there, as it does for any parameter with a custom loader.

## Accuracy Tests

The first load folds the same value as before, just at load time instead of on the first forward. Routing only changes after `scale` is reloaded.

New CPU test `test/registered/unit/models/test_gemma4_router_scale.py`: it loads `scale`, runs a forward, loads a new `scale` through `Gemma4ForCausalLM.load_weights`, and checks that `norm.weight` is `new_scale * root_size` and was updated in place. It fails on main, and it also fails if the loader only clears `_scale_fused`.

`test_gemma4_diffusion.py`, `test_gemma4_uniform_lifecycle.py`, `test_gemma4_renoise.py` and `test_gemma4_cuda_graph.py` in `test/registered/unit/dllm/` still pass on CPU.

Not run: an end-to-end online update on GPU, and the `--cpu-offload-gb` path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A, the forward is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A, see above)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -184,6 +184,7 @@ def __init__(
         )
         # Per-dimension learned scale, applied after norm + root_size
         self.scale = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(self.hidden_size))
+        self.scale.weight_loader = self._load_scale
         # Constant 1/sqrt(hidden_size) scaling factor
         self.register_buffer(
             "root_size",
@@ -202,10 +203,17 @@ def __init__(
 
     def fuse_scale(self):
         """Fold scale * root_size into norm.weight so forward needs no extra mul."""
-        fused = (self.scale * self.root_size).to(self.norm.weight.dtype)
+        # With --cpu-offload-gb, scale is on the CPU when loaded; the buffers are not.
+        scale = self.scale.to(self.root_size.device)
+        fused = (scale * self.root_size).to(self.norm.weight.dtype)
         self.norm.weight.data.copy_(fused)
         self._scale_fused = True
 
+    def _load_scale(self, param: nn.Parameter, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+        default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
+        # Refold here, not on the next forward: CUDA graph replay skips that check.
+        self.fuse_scale()
+
     def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
         """Returns raw router logits [T, E]."""
         if not self._scale_fused:

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+"""Regression test for Gemma 4 router scale updates after the first forward."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=11, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.models.gemma4_causal import Gemma4ForCausalLM, Gemma4Router
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+_CONFIG = SimpleNamespace(
+    hidden_size=8, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, num_experts=4, tie_word_embeddings=False
+)
+_SCALE_NAME = "model.layers.0.router.scale"
+
+
+def _causal_lm_with_router(router):
+    lm = Gemma4ForCausalLM.__new__(Gemma4ForCausalLM)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(lm)
+    lm.config = _CONFIG
+    lm.pp_group = SimpleNamespace(world_size=1)
+    lm.model = torch.nn.Module()
+    lm.model.start_layer, lm.model.end_layer = 0, 1
+    lm.model.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([torch.nn.Module()])
+    lm.model.layers[0].router = router
+    return lm
+
+
+class TestGemma4RouterScale(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_reloaded_scale_reaches_router_norm(self):
+        """A scale loaded after the first forward must reach the router norm weight."""
+        router = Gemma4Router(_CONFIG)
+        lm = _causal_lm_with_router(router)
+        norm_ptr = router.norm.weight.data_ptr()
+
+        lm.load_weights([(_SCALE_NAME, torch.full((8,), 2.0))])
+        router(torch.randn(3, 8))
+        updated = torch.full((8,), 5.0)
+        lm.load_weights([(_SCALE_NAME, updated)])
+
+        self.assertEqual(router.norm.weight.data_ptr(), norm_ptr)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(router.norm.weight, updated * router.root_size)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
